title: Cost you can see: each execution's token use priced by model, the cost per mission, task and agent over 24 h and 7 d on the page, a mission's daily budget alerting once
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard/transcripts.rs (how the scorecard already reads the engine's usage: one assistant message counts once per message id, across every line and copy that repeats it, at its earliest line's timestamp, under its `message.model`; the four token fields of `message.usage`), crates/spawn-core/src/ingest.rs (`claude_line`: how the Bridge reads an execution's transcript lines into events; `turn.stopped` carries `input_tokens` and `output_tokens`, always left unset today) and crates/spawn-host/src/transcripts.rs (the archive of each native session's transcript); crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (the routes, `/api/scorecard` and `/api/alerts` as read-only answers, BAD_REQUEST for a 400); crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs (the module comment: an alert fires once per occurrence, rests on a record or a reading, and is never fired twice whatever restarts; `memory_low` is a reading-based condition); crates/spawn-cli/src/missions.rs (`configure`'s budget flags `--minutes` and `--tool-calls`, the clearing switches) and crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (`mission_missions.budget`, `spawn_settings_merge`, `spawn_mission_configure`); web/src/scorecard.ts and, if present, web/src/scorecardFormat.ts (the scorecard's cost display: a cost that is not zero never reads as zero, GitHub #16 item 3), web/src/App.tsx and web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx (the pages and how one is reached); docs/fleet-architecture.md §3.4 (Alerts).

The problem. A Spawn user cannot see what the fleet costs. The engine writes each model call's usage to its transcript, and the scorecard reads it, but only as tokens per landing for the whole fleet: nothing records what an execution used, nothing turns tokens into money, and nothing says what a mission, a task or an agent cost today or this week. A mission can burn through a day's money with nobody told.

Required behaviour. (a) Recorded per execution: each assistant message in an execution's transcript (a line of `type` `assistant` with `message.id`, `message.model` and `message.usage`) counts once per message id, however many lines repeat it (Claude Code writes one line per content block, each with the same id and usage), with the largest usage of its lines, at its earliest line's `timestamp`, under its model: its input, output, cache creation (`cache_write`) and cache read tokens, and its cost. It counts for the execution whose transcript holds it, that execution's agent, the task the agent held at the message's time (its latest task assigned at or before that time; a message timed before any of the agent's tasks was assigned, as a line's clock may say, counts for the agent's latest task assigned at or before the execution started; none: no task, as the supervisor's) and that task's mission. What is recorded is kept in the database: a restarted loop or server counts no message twice and loses none, and a message is priced when it is recorded (a later price change does not rewrite past costs). (b) Prices: `SPAWN_MODEL_PRICES`, a JSON object from model name to `{"input", "output", "cache_write", "cache_read"}`, each US dollars per million tokens, a number not below zero. A message's cost is the sum of each of its token counts times its rate over a million. A model the setting does not price counts its tokens and no cost: its `usd` is null, and its tokens are counted as unpriced, never as $0. Unset, a built-in table (in the code, its rates named in the docs) may price the models the fleet runs; set, the setting replaces it whole. A value that is not such an object (not JSON, a rate missing, negative or not a number) stops `spawn loop` and `spawn serve` at start, non-zero, with a message naming SPAWN_MODEL_PRICES. (c) Served: `GET /api/cost?window=24h` and `?window=7d` (24h when absent; any other window 400) answer the messages timed in [now minus the window, now): `{window, since_ms, until_ms, total, models, missions, tasks, agents, executions}`. `total` is `{usd, tokens, unpriced_tokens}`; `tokens` is always `{input, output, cache_write, cache_read}` (integers, every message, priced or not); `unpriced_tokens` the sum of the four counts of messages under an unpriced model. `models` lists `{model, usd, tokens}` (`usd` null for an unpriced model); `missions` `{mission, usd, tokens, unpriced_tokens}`; `tasks` `{task, mission, usd, tokens, unpriced_tokens}`; `agents` `{agent, usd, tokens, unpriced_tokens}`; `executions` `{execution, agent, task, usd, tokens, unpriced_tokens, models: [{model, usd, tokens}]}`. Ids are the store's (a mission and a task as numbers, an agent and an execution as strings). `usd` is a number, the exact sum (no rounding to cents in the answer), 0 for an entry with only unpriced messages; an entry with no message in the window is not listed. (d) Shown: web/src/cost.ts exports `formatUsd(usd: number | null): string` and `costView(answer)`. formatUsd: null reads "—", zero "$0.00", an amount that would round to $0.00 but is not zero "<$0.01" (the scorecard's rule: a cost that is not zero never reads as zero), any other the amount rounded to the cent with a dollar sign and thousands grouped ("$0.94", "$1,234.57"). costView returns `{total: string, unpriced: boolean, missions: Row[], tasks: Row[], agents: Row[]}` with `Row = {key: string, usd: string, unpriced: boolean}`: key `#<mission>`, `T<task>`, or the agent id; usd its formatUsd, except that an entry with unpriced tokens and no priced use reads "unpriced" (never "$0.00": it cost something no price says); `unpriced` true for an entry (and, at the top, the total) with any unpriced tokens; rows most costly first. The page marks unpriced use where it shows a figure. A Cost page, reached from the sidebar, shows costView's figures for 24 h and for 7 d (the total; each mission, task and agent). cost.ts and everything it imports must load with node alone (type stripping, no bundler, no packages): relative imports that name their `.ts` file, `import type` for anything used only as a type, no package imports, and only erasable TypeScript (no enum, namespace or parameter property). (e) The budget: `spawn mission configure --id <mission> --daily-usd <amount>` (a decimal above zero) records `budget.daily_usd` on the mission, and `--no-daily-usd` clears it, as `--minutes` and `--tool-calls` do. The alerts step raises a condition `cost_budget`, subject `mission #<id>`, key `cost_budget:<mission>:<the UTC day, YYYY-MM-DD>`, evidence the day's spend and the budget, text as "mission #4 spent $0.94 today (UTC), over its $0.50 daily budget", when, at one of the step's readings (every SPAWN_ALERT_CHECK_SECS), the mission's cost of messages timed in the current UTC day has reached its daily budget: once per mission and day, whatever restarts and however much more it spends; it clears when the day ends, or when the budget is removed or raised above the day's spend. A mission with no daily budget, or under it, raises none. It reaches the alerts API and home's "Needs you" as any open alert does. Keep the scorecard's cost dimension as it is; do not change its rule.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/041.sh (read its header): a real loop on a fake engine whose workers report known usage, priced by a SPAWN_MODEL_PRICES with two priced models and one unpriced, and `spawn serve` on a loopback port; (1) per execution, the repeated lines counted once, by model, a message timed before its task was assigned counted for that task, the unpriced model's tokens with no cost, a worker that ran only on it costing $0 with its tokens unpriced; (2) the daily budgets set with `--daily-usd`; no alert while under today, though over in 7 d; exactly one `cost_budget` alert once crossed, served by the alerts API; none for the mission under its budget; (3) the totals per mission, task, agent and model over 24 h and 7 d, each within $0.000001, a message timed 3 days ago in 7 d only; `?window=30d` 400; (4) web/src/cost.ts's `costView` given those answers shows each figure to the cent, a cost under a cent as "<$0.01", the worker that ran only on the unpriced model as "unpriced", and marks unpriced use; (5) the loop and serve restarted with one model's rates doubled: the totals are unchanged (priced when recorded, nothing counted twice), new spending on that model is priced at the new rates and added once, still one alert; (6) SPAWN_MODEL_PRICES not JSON or with a negative rate stops `spawn loop` and `spawn serve`, naming it. It fails at (1) on the live main (6ff6590e): `GET /api/cost` answers 404.

What it saves. The owner sees what each mission, task and agent costs today and this week, in dollars, on the page they already watch, and is told once when a mission goes over its daily money, instead of adding up tokens from transcripts by hand, or finding out from the bill.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
